[package.metadata.system-deps.libfoo]
version = "0.1"
fallback-names = ["libfoo-0.1"]
v1 = { version = "1.0", fallback-names = ["libfoo1"] }
v2 = { version = "2.0", fallback-names = ["libfoo2"] }
```
[§](https://docs.rs#feature-versions)Feature versions

`-sys` crates willing to support various versions of their underlying system libraries
can use features to control the version of the dependency required.
`system-deps` will pick the highest version among enabled features.
Such version features must use the pattern `v1_0`, `v1_2`, etc.

```
[features]
v1_2 = []
v1_4 = ["v1_2"]
v1_6 = ["v1_4"]
[package.metadata.system-deps.gstreamer_1_0]
name = "gstreamer-1.0"
version = "1.0"
v1_2 = { version = "1.2" }
v1_4 = { version = "1.4" }
v1_6 = { version = "1.6" }
```
The same mechanism can be used to require a different library name depending on the version:

```
[package.metadata.system-deps.gst_gl]
name = "gstreamer-gl-1.0"
version = "1.14"
v1_18 = { version = "1.18", name = "gstreamer-gl-egl-1.0" }
```
[§](https://docs.rs#target-specific-dependencies)Target specific dependencies

You can define target specific dependencies:

```
[package.metadata.system-deps.'cfg(target_os = "linux")']
testdata = "1"
[package.metadata.system-deps.'cfg(not(target_os = "macos"))']
testlib = "1"
[package.metadata.system-deps.'cfg(unix)']
testanotherlib = { version = "1", optional = true }
```
See [the Rust documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/conditional-compilation.html)
for the exact syntax.
Currently, those keys are supported:

- `target_arch`
- `target_endian`
- `target_env`
- `target_family`
- `target_os`
- `target_pointer_width`
- `target_vendor`
- `unix`and- `windows`

[§](https://docs.rs#overriding-build-flags)Overriding build flags

By default `system-deps` automatically defines the required build flags for each dependency using the information fetched from `pkg-config`.
These flags can be overridden using environment variables if needed:

- `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_SEARCH_NATIVE`to override the- `cargo:rustc-link-search=native`
- `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_SEARCH_FRAMEWORK`to override the- `cargo:rustc-link-search=framework`
- `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_LIB`to override the- `cargo:rustc-link-lib`
- `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_LIB_FRAMEWORK`to override the- `cargo:rustc-link-lib=framework`
- `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_INCLUDE`to override the- `cargo:include`

With `$NAME` being the upper case name of the key defining the dependency in `Cargo.toml`.
For example `SYSTEM_DEPS_TESTLIB_SEARCH_NATIVE=/opt/lib` could be used to override a dependency named `testlib`.

One can also define the environment variable `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_NO_PKG_CONFIG` to fully disable `pkg-config` lookup
for the given dependency. In this case at least SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_LIB or SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_LIB_FRAMEWORK should be defined as well.

[§](https://docs.rs#internally-build-system-libraries)Internally build system libraries

`-sys` crates can provide support for building and statically link their underlying system library as part of their build process.
Here is how to do this in your `build.rs`:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
fn main() {
    system_deps::Config::new()
        .add_build_internal("testlib", |lib, version| {
            // Actually build the library here that fulfills the passed in version requirements
            system_deps::Library::from_internal_pkg_config("build/path-to-pc-file", lib, "1.2.4")
         })
        .probe()
        .unwrap();
}
```
This feature can be controlled using the `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_BUILD_INTERNAL` environment variable
which can have the following values:

- `auto`: build the dependency only if the required version has not been found by- `pkg-config`;
- `always`: always build the dependency, ignoring any version which may be installed on the system;
- `never`: (default) never build the dependency,- `system-deps`will fail if the required version is not found on the system.

You can also use the `SYSTEM_DEPS_BUILD_INTERNAL` environment variable with the same values
defining the behavior for all the dependencies which don’t have `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_BUILD_INTERNAL` defined.

[§](https://docs.rs#static-linking)Static linking

By default all libraries are dynamically linked, except when build internally as [described above](https://docs.rs#internally-build-system-libraries).
Libraries can be statically linked by defining the environment variable `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_LINK=static`.
You can also use `SYSTEM_DEPS_LINK=static` to statically link all the libraries.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Config](https://docs.rs/struct.Config.html)
- Structure used to configure `metadata`before starting to probe for dependencies
- [Dependencies](https://docs.rs/struct.Dependencies.html)
- All the system dependencies retrieved by `Config::probe`
- [Internal](https://docs.rs/struct.InternalLib.html)- Lib
- Internal library name and if a static library is available on the system
- [Library](https://docs.rs/struct.Library.html)
- A system dependency

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Build](https://docs.rs/enum.BuildInternalClosureError.html)- Internal - Closure - Error
- Error used in return value of `Config::add_build_internal`closures
- [Error](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html)
- system-deps errors
- [Source](https://docs.rs/enum.Source.html)
- From where the library settings have been retrieved

# system_deps - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/system-deps/7.0.8/target-redirect/system_deps/

## Expand description

`system-deps` lets you write system dependencies in `Cargo.toml` metadata,
rather than programmatically in `build.rs`. This makes those dependencies
declarative, so other tools can read them as well.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

In your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[build-dependencies]
system-deps = "2.0"
```
Then, to declare a dependency on `testlib >= 1.2`
add the following section:

```
[package.metadata.system-deps]
testlib = "1.2"
```
Finally, in your `build.rs`, add:

[§](https://docs.rs#version-format)Version format

Versions can be expressed in the following formats

- “1.2” or “>= 1.2”: At least version 1.2
- “>= 1.2, < 2.0”: At least version 1.2 but less than version 2.0

In the future more complicated version expressions might be supported.

Note that these versions are not interpreted according to the semver rules, but based on the rules defined by pkg-config.

[§](https://docs.rs#feature-specific-dependency)Feature-specific dependency

You can easily declare an optional system dependency by associating it with a feature:

```
[package.metadata.system-deps]
testdata = { version = "4.5", feature = "use-testdata" }
```
`system-deps` will check for `testdata` only if the `use-testdata` feature has been enabled.

[§](https://docs.rs#optional-dependency)Optional dependency

Another option is to use the `optional` setting, which can also be used using [features versions](https://docs.rs#feature-versions):

```
[package.metadata.system-deps]
test-data = { version = "4.5", optional = true }
testmore = { version = "2", v3 = { version = "3.0", optional = true }}
```
`system-deps` will automatically export for each dependency a feature `system_deps_have_$DEP` where `$DEP`
is the `toml` key defining the dependency in [snake_case](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snake_case).
This can be used to check if an optional dependency has been found or not:

```
#[cfg(system_deps_have_testdata)]
println!("found test-data");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#overriding-library-name)Overriding library name

`toml` keys cannot contain dot characters so if your library name does, you can define it using the `name` field:

```
[package.metadata.system-deps]
glib = { name = "glib-2.0", version = "2.64" }
```
[§](https://docs.rs#fallback-library-names)Fallback library names

Some libraries may be available under different names on different platforms or distributions. To allow for this, you can define fallback names to search for if the main library name does not work.

```
[package.metadata.system-deps]
aravis = { fallback-names = ["aravis-0.8"] }
```
You may also specify different fallback names for different versions:

```
[package.metadata.system-deps.libfoo]
version = "0.1"
fallback-names = ["libfoo-0.1"]
v1 = { version = "1.0", fallback-names = ["libfoo1"] }
v2 = { version = "2.0", fallback-names = ["libfoo2"] }
```
[§](https://docs.rs#feature-versions)Feature versions

`-sys` crates willing to support various versions of their underlying system libraries
can use features to control the version of the dependency required.
`system-deps` will pick the highest version among enabled features.
Such version features must use the pattern `v1_0`, `v1_2`, etc.

```
[features]
v1_2 = []
v1_4 = ["v1_2"]
v1_6 = ["v1_4"]
[package.metadata.system-deps.gstreamer_1_0]
name = "gstreamer-1.0"
version = "1.0"
v1_2 = { version = "1.2" }
v1_4 = { version = "1.4" }
v1_6 = { version = "1.6" }
```
The same mechanism can be used to require a different library name depending on the version:

```
[package.metadata.system-deps.gst_gl]
name = "gstreamer-gl-1.0"
version = "1.14"
v1_18 = { version = "1.18", name = "gstreamer-gl-egl-1.0" }
```
[§](https://docs.rs#target-specific-dependencies)Target specific dependencies

You can define target specific dependencies:

```
[package.metadata.system-deps.'cfg(target_os = "linux")']
testdata = "1"
[package.metadata.system-deps.'cfg(not(target_os = "macos"))']
testlib = "1"
[package.metadata.system-deps.'cfg(unix)']
testanotherlib = { version = "1", optional = true }
```
See [the Rust documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/conditional-compilation.html)
for the exact syntax.
Currently, those keys are supported:

- `target_arch`
- `target_endian`
- `target_env`
- `target_family`
- `target_os`
- `target_pointer_width`
- `target_vendor`
- `unix`and- `windows`

[§](https://docs.rs#overriding-build-flags)Overriding build flags

By default `system-deps` automatically defines the required build flags for each dependency using the information fetched from `pkg-config`.
These flags can be overridden using environment variables if needed:

- `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_SEARCH_NATIVE`to override the- `cargo:rustc-link-search=native`
- `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_SEARCH_FRAMEWORK`to override the- `cargo:rustc-link-search=framework`
- `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_LIB`to override the- `cargo:rustc-link-lib`
- `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_LIB_FRAMEWORK`to override the- `cargo:rustc-link-lib=framework`
- `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_INCLUDE`to override the- `cargo:include`

With `$NAME` being the upper case name of the key defining the dependency in `Cargo.toml`.
For example `SYSTEM_DEPS_TESTLIB_SEARCH_NATIVE=/opt/lib` could be used to override a dependency named `testlib`.

One can also define the environment variable `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_NO_PKG_CONFIG` to fully disable `pkg-config` lookup
for the given dependency. In this case at least SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_LIB or SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_LIB_FRAMEWORK should be defined as well.

[§](https://docs.rs#internally-build-system-libraries)Internally build system libraries

`-sys` crates can provide support for building and statically link their underlying system library as part of their build process.
Here is how to do this in your `build.rs`:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```

    system_deps::Config::new()
        .add_build_internal("testlib", |lib, version| {
            // Actually build the library here that fulfills the passed in version requirements
            system_deps::Library::from_internal_pkg_config("build/path-to-pc-file", lib, "1.2.4")
         })
        .probe()
        .unwrap();
}
```
This feature can be controlled using the `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_BUILD_INTERNAL` environment variable
which can have the following values:

- `auto`: build the dependency only if the required version has not been found by- `pkg-config`;
- `always`: always build the dependency, ignoring any version which may be installed on the system;
- `never`: (default) never build the dependency,- `system-deps`will fail if the required version is not found on the system.

You can also use the `SYSTEM_DEPS_BUILD_INTERNAL` environment variable with the same values
defining the behavior for all the dependencies which don’t have `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_BUILD_INTERNAL` defined.

[§](https://docs.rs#static-linking)Static linking

By default all libraries are dynamically linked, except when build internally as [described above](https://docs.rs#internally-build-system-libraries).
Libraries can be statically linked by defining the environment variable `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_LINK=static`.
You can also use `SYSTEM_DEPS_LINK=static` to statically link all the libraries.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Config](https://docs.rs/struct.Config.html)
- Structure used to configure `metadata`before starting to probe for dependencies
- [Dependencies](https://docs.rs/struct.Dependencies.html)
- All the system dependencies retrieved by `Config::probe`
- [Internal](https://docs.rs/struct.InternalLib.html)- Lib

- system-deps errors

- From where the library settings have been retrieved

Source: https://docs.rs/system-deps/7.0.8/system_deps/index.html

[273](#273)impl fmt::Display for Error {
[274](#274)    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
[275](#275)        match self {
[276](#276)            Self::PkgConfig(e) => write!(f, "{e}"),
[277](#277)            Self::BuildInternalClosureError(s, e) => write!(f, "Failed to build {s}: {e}"),
[278](#278)            Self::FailToRead(s, _) => write!(f, "{s}"),
[279](#279)            Self::InvalidMetadata(s) => write!(f, "{s}"),
[280](#280)            Self::MissingLib(s) => write!(
[281](#281)                f,
[282](#282)                "You should define at least one lib using {} or {}",
[283](#283)                EnvVariable::new_lib(s),
[284](#284)                EnvVariable::new_lib_framework(s),
[285](#285)            ),
[286](#286)            Self::BuildInternalInvalid(s) => write!(f, "{s}"),
[287](#287)            Self::BuildInternalNoClosure(s1, s2) => {
[288](#288)                write!(f, "Missing build internal closure for {s1} (version {s2})")
[289](#289)            }
[290](#290)            Self::BuildInternalWrongVersion(s1, s2, s3) => write!(
[291](#291)                f,
[292](#292)                "Internally built {s1} {s2} but minimum required version is {s3}"
[293](#293)            ),
[294](#294)            Self::UnsupportedCfg(s) => write!(f, "Unsupported cfg() expression: {s}"),
[295](#295)        }
[296](#296)    }
[297](#297)}
[298](#298)
[299](#299)#[derive(Debug, Default)]
[300](#300)pub struct Dependencies {

[305](#305)impl Dependencies {

[315](#315)    pub fn iter(&self) -> Vec<(&str, &Library)> {
[319](#319)        let mut v = self
[320](#320)            .libs
[321](#321)            .iter()
[322](#322)            .map(|(k, v)| (k.as_str(), v))
[323](#323)            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
[324](#324)        v.sort_by_key(|x| x.0);
[325](#325)        v
[326](#326)    }
[327](#327)

[336](#336)        v.dedup();
[337](#337)        v

[407](#407)
[408](#408)    fn override_from_flags(&mut self, env: &EnvVariables) {
[409](#409)        for (name, lib) in self.libs.iter_mut() {
[410](#410)            if let Some(value) = env.get(&EnvVariable::new_search_native(name)) {
[411](#411)                lib.link_paths = split_paths(&value);
[412](#412)            }
[413](#413)            if let Some(value) = env.get(&EnvVariable::new_search_framework(name)) {
[414](#414)                lib.framework_paths = split_paths(&value);
[415](#415)            }
[416](#416)            if let Some(value) = env.get(&EnvVariable::new_lib(name)) {
[417](#417)                let should_be_linked_statically = env
[418](#418)                    .has_value(&EnvVariable::new_link(Some(name)), "static")
[419](#419)                    || env.has_value(&EnvVariable::new_link(None), "static");
[420](#420)
[421](#421)                let is_static_lib_available = should_be_linked_statically;
[425](#425)
[426](#426)                lib.libs = split_string(&value)
[427](#427)                    .into_iter()
[428](#428)                    .map(|l| InternalLib::new(l, is_static_lib_available))
[429](#429)                    .collect();
[430](#430)            }
[431](#431)            if let Some(value) = env.get(&EnvVariable::new_lib_framework(name)) {
[432](#432)                lib.frameworks = split_string(&value);
[433](#433)            }
[434](#434)            if let Some(value) = env.get(&EnvVariable::new_include(name)) {
[435](#435)                lib.include_paths = split_paths(&value);
[436](#436)            }
[437](#437)            if let Some(value) = env.get(&EnvVariable::new_linker_args(name)) {
[438](#438)                lib.ld_args = split_string(&value)
[439](#439)                    .into_iter()
[440](#440)                    .map(|l| l.split(',').map(|l| l.to_string()).collect())
[441](#441)                    .collect();
[442](#442)            }
[443](#443)        }
[444](#444)    }
[445](#445)
[446](#446)    fn gen_flags(&self) -> Result<BuildFlags, Error> {
[447](#447)        let mut flags = BuildFlags::new();
[448](#448)        let mut include_paths = Vec::new();
[449](#449)
[450](#450)        for (name, lib) in self.iter() {
[451](#451)            include_paths.extend(lib.include_paths.clone());
[452](#452)
[453](#453)            if lib.source == Source::EnvVariables
[454](#454)                && lib.libs.is_empty()
[455](#455)                && lib.frameworks.is_empty()
[456](#456)            {
[457](#457)                return Err(Error::MissingLib(name.to_string()));
[458](#458)            }
[459](#459)
[460](#460)            lib.link_paths
[461](#461)                .iter()
[462](#462)                .for_each(|l| flags.add(BuildFlag::SearchNative(l.to_string_lossy().to_string())));
[463](#463)            lib.framework_paths.iter().for_each(|f| {
[464](#464)                flags.add(BuildFlag::SearchFramework(f.to_string_lossy().to_string()))
[465](#465)            });
[466](#466)            lib.libs.iter().for_each(|l| {
[467](#467)                flags.add(BuildFlag::Lib(
[468](#468)                    l.name.clone(),
[469](#469)                    lib.statik && l.is_static_available,
[470](#470)                ))
[471](#471)            });
[472](#472)            lib.frameworks
[473](#473)                .iter()
[474](#474)                .for_each(|f| flags.add(BuildFlag::LibFramework(f.clone())));
[475](#475)            lib.ld_args
[476](#476)                .iter()
[477](#477)                .for_each(|f| flags.add(BuildFlag::LinkArg(f.clone())))
[478](#478)        }
[479](#479)
[480](#480)        if !include_paths.is_empty() {
[483](#483)            if let Ok(paths) = std::env::join_paths(include_paths) {
[484](#484)                flags.add(BuildFlag::Include(paths.to_string_lossy().to_string()));
[485](#485)            }
[486](#486)        }
[487](#487)
[488](#488)        flags.add(BuildFlag::RerunIfEnvChanged(
[490](#490)            EnvVariable::new_build_internal(None),
[491](#491)        ));
[492](#492)        flags.add(BuildFlag::RerunIfEnvChanged(EnvVariable::new_link(None)));
[493](#493)
[494](#494)        for (name, _lib) in self.libs.iter() {
[495](#495)            EnvVariable::set_rerun_if_changed_for_all_variants(&mut flags, name);
[496](#496)        }
[497](#497)
[498](#498)        Ok(flags)
[499](#499)    }
[500](#500)}
[501](#501)

[549](#549)enum EnvVariable {

[561](#561)impl EnvVariable {

[566](#566)    fn new_lib_framework(lib: &str) -> Self {

[568](#568)    }

[572](#572)    }

[576](#576)    }

[579](#579)        Self::Include(lib.to_string())
[580](#580)    }

[597](#597)
[598](#598)    const fn suffix(&self) -> &'static str {
[599](#599)        match self {
[600](#600)            EnvVariable::Lib(_) => "LIB",
[601](#601)            EnvVariable::LibFramework(_) => "LIB_FRAMEWORK",
[602](#602)            EnvVariable::SearchNative(_) => "SEARCH_NATIVE",
[603](#603)            EnvVariable::SearchFramework(_) => "SEARCH_FRAMEWORK",
[604](#604)            EnvVariable::Include(_) => "INCLUDE",
[605](#605)            EnvVariable::NoPkgConfig(_) => "NO_PKG_CONFIG",
[606](#606)            EnvVariable::BuildInternal(_) => "BUILD_INTERNAL",
[607](#607)            EnvVariable::Link(_) => "LINK",
[608](#608)            EnvVariable::LinkerArgs(_) => "LDFLAGS",
[609](#609)        }
[610](#610)    }
[611](#611)
[612](#612)    fn set_rerun_if_changed_for_all_variants(flags: &mut BuildFlags, name: &str) {
[613](#613)        #[inline]
[614](#614)        fn add_to_flags(flags: &mut BuildFlags, var: EnvVariable) {
[615](#615)            flags.add(BuildFlag::RerunIfEnvChanged(var));
[616](#616)        }
[617](#617)        add_to_flags(flags, EnvVariable::new_lib(name));
[618](#618)        add_to_flags(flags, EnvVariable::new_lib_framework(name));
[619](#619)        add_to_flags(flags, EnvVariable::new_search_native(name));
[620](#620)        add_to_flags(flags, EnvVariable::new_search_framework(name));
[621](#621)        add_to_flags(flags, EnvVariable::new_include(name));
[622](#622)        add_to_flags(flags, EnvVariable::new_linker_args(name));
[623](#623)        add_to_flags(flags, EnvVariable::new_no_pkg_config(name));
[624](#624)        add_to_flags(flags, EnvVariable::new_build_internal(Some(name)));
[625](#625)        add_to_flags(flags, EnvVariable::new_link(Some(name)));
[626](#626)    }
[627](#627)}
[628](#628)
[629](#629)impl fmt::Display for EnvVariable {
[630](#630)    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
[631](#631)        let suffix = match self {
[632](#632)            EnvVariable::Lib(lib)
[633](#633)            | EnvVariable::LibFramework(lib)
[634](#634)            | EnvVariable::SearchNative(lib)
[635](#635)            | EnvVariable::SearchFramework(lib)
[636](#636)            | EnvVariable::Include(lib)
[637](#637)            | EnvVariable::LinkerArgs(lib)
[638](#638)            | EnvVariable::NoPkgConfig(lib)
[639](#639)            | EnvVariable::BuildInternal(Some(lib))
[640](#640)            | EnvVariable::Link(Some(lib)) => {
[641](#641)                format!("{}_{}", lib.to_shouty_snake_case(), self.suffix())
[642](#642)            }
[643](#643)            EnvVariable::BuildInternal(None) | EnvVariable::Link(None) => self.suffix().to_string(),
[644](#644)        };
[645](#645)        write!(f, "SYSTEM_DEPS_{suffix}")
[646](#646)    }

[649](#649)type FnBuildInternal =
[650](#650)    dyn FnOnce(&str, &str) -> std::result::Result<Library, BuildInternalClosureError>;
[651](#651)
[652](#652)pub struct Config {
[654](#654)    env: EnvVariables,
[655](#655)    build_internals: HashMap<String, Box<FnBuildInternal>>,
[656](#656)}
[657](#657)
[658](#658)impl Default for Config {
[659](#659)    fn default() -> Self {
[660](#660)        Self::new_with_env(EnvVariables::Environment)
[661](#661)    }
[662](#662)}
[663](#663)
[664](#664)impl Config {
[665](#665)    pub fn new() -> Self {
[667](#667)        Self::default()
[668](#668)    }
[669](#669)
[670](#670)    fn new_with_env(env: EnvVariables) -> Self {
[671](#671)        Self {
[672](#672)            env,
[673](#673)            build_internals: HashMap::new(),
[674](#674)        }
[675](#675)    }
[676](#676)
[677](#677)    pub fn probe(self) -> Result<Dependencies, Error> {
[682](#682)        let libraries = self.probe_full()?;
[683](#683)        let flags = libraries.gen_flags()?;
[684](#684)
[685](#685)        println!("{flags}");
[687](#687)
[688](#688)        for (name, _) in libraries.iter() {
[689](#689)            println!("cargo:rustc-cfg=system_deps_have_{}", name.to_snake_case());
[690](#690)        }
[691](#691)
[692](#692)        Ok(libraries)
[693](#693)    }
[694](#694)
[695](#695)    pub fn add_build_internal<F>(self, name: &str, func: F) -> Self
[708](#708)    where
[709](#709)        F: 'static + FnOnce(&str, &str) -> std::result::Result<Library, BuildInternalClosureError>,
[710](#710)    {
[711](#711)        let mut build_internals = self.build_internals;
[712](#712)        build_internals.insert(name.to_string(), Box::new(func));
[713](#713)
[714](#714)        Self {
[715](#715)            env: self.env,
[716](#716)            build_internals,
[717](#717)        }
[718](#718)    }
[719](#719)
[720](#720)    fn probe_full(mut self) -> Result<Dependencies, Error> {
[721](#721)        let mut libraries = self.probe_pkg_config()?;
[722](#722)        libraries.override_from_flags(&self.env);
[723](#723)
[724](#724)        Ok(libraries)
[725](#725)    }
[726](#726)
[727](#727)    fn probe_pkg_config(&mut self) -> Result<Dependencies, Error> {
[728](#728)        let dir = self
[729](#729)            .env
[730](#730)            .get("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")
[731](#731)            .ok_or_else(|| Error::InvalidMetadata("$CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR not set".into()))?;
[732](#732)        let mut path = PathBuf::from(dir);
[733](#733)        path.push("Cargo.toml");
[734](#734)
[735](#735)        println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed={}", &path.to_string_lossy());
[736](#736)
[737](#737)        let metadata = MetaData::from_file(&path)?;
[738](#738)
[739](#739)        let mut libraries = Dependencies::default();
[740](#740)
[741](#741)        for dep in metadata.deps.iter() {
[742](#742)            if let Some(cfg) = &dep.cfg {
[743](#743)                if !self.check_cfg(cfg)? {
[745](#745)                    continue;
[746](#746)                }
[747](#747)            }
[748](#748)
[749](#749)            let mut enabled_feature_overrides = Vec::new();
[750](#750)
[751](#751)            for o in dep.version_overrides.iter() {
[752](#752)                if self.has_feature(&o.key) {
[753](#753)                    enabled_feature_overrides.push(o);
[754](#754)                }
[755](#755)            }
[756](#756)
[757](#757)            if let Some(feature) = dep.feature.as_ref() {
[758](#758)                if !self.has_feature(feature) {
[759](#759)                    continue;
[760](#760)                }
[761](#761)            }
[762](#762)
[763](#763)            let version;
[765](#765)            let lib_name;
[766](#766)            let fallback_lib_names;
[767](#767)            let optional;
[768](#768)            if enabled_feature_overrides.is_empty() {
[769](#769)                version = dep.version.as_deref();
[770](#770)                lib_name = dep.lib_name();
[771](#771)                fallback_lib_names = dep.fallback_names.as_deref().unwrap_or(&[]);
[772](#772)                optional = dep.optional;
[773](#773)            } else {
[774](#774)                enabled_feature_overrides.sort_by(|a, b| {
[775](#775)                    fn min_version(r: metadata::VersionRange<'_>) -> &str {
[776](#776)                        match r.start_bound() {
[777](#777)                            std::ops::Bound::Unbounded => unreachable!(),
[778](#778)                            std::ops::Bound::Excluded(_) => unreachable!(),
[779](#779)                            std::ops::Bound::Included(b) => b,
[780](#780)                        }
[781](#781)                    }
[782](#782)
[783](#783)                    let a = min_version(metadata::parse_version(&a.version));
[784](#784)                    let b = min_version(metadata::parse_version(&b.version));
[785](#785)
[786](#786)                    version_compare::compare(a, b)
[787](#787)                        .expect("failed to compare versions")
[788](#788)                        .ord()
[789](#789)                        .expect("invalid version")
[790](#790)                });
[791](#791)                let highest = enabled_feature_overrides.into_iter().next_back().unwrap();
[792](#792)
[793](#793)                version = Some(highest.version.as_str());
[794](#794)                lib_name = highest.name.as_deref().unwrap_or(dep.lib_name());
[795](#795)                fallback_lib_names = highest
[796](#796)                    .fallback_names
[797](#797)                    .as_deref()
[798](#798)                    .or(dep.fallback_names.as_deref())
[799](#799)                    .unwrap_or(&[]);
[800](#800)                optional = highest.optional.unwrap_or(dep.optional);
[801](#801)            };
[802](#802)
[803](#803)            let version = version.ok_or_else(|| {
[804](#804)                Error::InvalidMetadata(format!("No version defined for {}", dep.key))
[805](#805)            })?;
[806](#806)
[807](#807)            let name = &dep.key;
[808](#808)            let build_internal = self.get_build_internal_status(name)?;
[809](#809)
[810](#810)            let statik = self
[812](#812)                .env
[813](#813)                .has_value(&EnvVariable::new_link(Some(name)), "static")
[814](#814)                || self.env.has_value(&EnvVariable::new_link(None), "static");
[815](#815)
[816](#816)            let mut library = if self.env.contains(&EnvVariable::new_no_pkg_config(name)) {
[817](#817)                Library::from_env_variables(name)
[818](#818)            } else if build_internal == BuildInternal::Always {
[819](#819)                self.call_build_internal(lib_name, version)?
[820](#820)            } else {
[821](#821)                let mut config = pkg_config::Config::new();
[822](#822)                config
[823](#823)                    .print_system_libs(false)
[824](#824)                    .cargo_metadata(false)
[825](#825)                    .range_version(metadata::parse_version(version))
[826](#826)                    .statik(statik);
[827](#827)
[828](#828)                match Self::probe_with_fallback(config, lib_name, fallback_lib_names) {
[829](#829)                    Ok((lib_name, lib)) => Library::from_pkg_config(lib_name, lib),
[830](#830)                    Err(e) => {
[831](#831)                        if build_internal == BuildInternal::Auto {
[832](#832)                            self.call_build_internal(name, version)?
[834](#834)                        } else if optional {
[835](#835)                            continue;
[837](#837)                        } else {
[838](#838)                            return Err(e.into());
[839](#839)                        }
[840](#840)                    }
[841](#841)                }
[842](#842)            };
[843](#843)
[844](#844)            library.statik = statik;
[845](#845)
[846](#846)            libraries.add(name, library);
[847](#847)        }
[848](#848)        Ok(libraries)
[849](#849)    }

[851](#851)    fn probe_with_fallback<'a>(
[852](#852)        config: pkg_config::Config,
[853](#853)        name: &'a str,
[854](#854)        fallback_names: &'a [String],
[855](#855)    ) -> Result<(&'a str, pkg_config::Library), pkg_config::Error> {
[856](#856)        let error = match config.probe(name) {
[857](#857)            Ok(x) => return Ok((name, x)),
[858](#858)            Err(e) => e,
[859](#859)        };
[860](#860)        for name in fallback_names {
[861](#861)            if let Ok(library) = config.probe(name) {
[862](#862)                return Ok((name, library));
[863](#863)            }
[864](#864)        }
[865](#865)        Err(error)
[866](#866)    }

[891](#891)    fn call_build_internal(&mut self, name: &str, version_str: &str) -> Result<Library, Error> {
[892](#892)        let lib = match self.build_internals.remove(name) {
[893](#893)            Some(f) => f(name, version_str)
[894](#894)                .map_err(|e| Error::BuildInternalClosureError(name.into(), e))?,
[895](#895)            None => {
[896](#896)                return Err(Error::BuildInternalNoClosure(
[897](#897)                    name.into(),
[898](#898)                    version_str.into(),
[899](#899)                ))
[900](#900)            }
[901](#901)        };
[902](#902)
[903](#903)        let version = metadata::parse_version(version_str);
[905](#905)        fn min_version(r: metadata::VersionRange<'_>) -> &str {
[906](#906)            match r.start_bound() {
[907](#907)                std::ops::Bound::Unbounded => unreachable!(),
[908](#908)                std::ops::Bound::Excluded(_) => unreachable!(),
[909](#909)                std::ops::Bound::Included(b) => b,
[910](#910)            }
[911](#911)        }
[912](#912)        fn max_version(r: metadata::VersionRange<'_>) -> Option<&str> {
[913](#913)            match r.end_bound() {
[914](#914)                std::ops::Bound::Included(_) => unreachable!(),
[915](#915)                std::ops::Bound::Unbounded => None,
[916](#916)                std::ops::Bound::Excluded(b) => Some(*b),
[917](#917)            }
[918](#918)        }
[919](#919)
[920](#920)        let min = min_version(version.clone());
[921](#921)        if version_compare::compare(&lib.version, min) == Ok(version_compare::Cmp::Lt) {
[922](#922)            return Err(Error::BuildInternalWrongVersion(
[923](#923)                name.into(),
[924](#924)                lib.version,
[925](#925)                version_str.into(),
[926](#926)            ));
[927](#927)        }
[928](#928)
[929](#929)        if let Some(max) = max_version(version) {
[930](#930)            if version_compare::compare(&lib.version, max) == Ok(version_compare::Cmp::Ge) {
[931](#931)                return Err(Error::BuildInternalWrongVersion(
[932](#932)                    name.into(),
[933](#933)                    lib.version,
[934](#934)                    version_str.into(),
[935](#935)                ));
[936](#936)            }
[937](#937)        }
[938](#938)
[939](#939)        Ok(lib)
[940](#940)    }
[941](#941)
[942](#942)    fn has_feature(&self, feature: &str) -> bool {

[947](#947)    fn check_cfg(&self, cfg: &cfg_expr::Expression) -> Result<bool, Error> {
[948](#948)        use cfg_expr::{targets::get_builtin_target_by_triple, Predicate};
[949](#949)
[950](#950)        let target = self
[951](#951)            .env
[952](#952)            .get("TARGET")
[953](#953)            .expect("no TARGET env variable defined");
[954](#954)
[955](#955)        let res = if let Some(target) = get_builtin_target_by_triple(&target) {
[956](#956)            cfg.eval(|pred| match pred {
[957](#957)                Predicate::Target(tp) => Some(tp.matches(target)),
[958](#958)                _ => None,
[959](#959)            })
[960](#960)        } else {
[961](#961)            let triple: cfg_expr::target_lexicon::Triple = target.parse().unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("TARGET {} is not a builtin target, and it could not be parsed as a valid triplet: {}", target, e));
[963](#963)
[964](#964)            cfg.eval(|pred| match pred {
[965](#965)                Predicate::Target(tp) => Some(tp.matches(&triple)),
[966](#966)                _ => None,
[967](#967)            })
[968](#968)        };
[969](#969)
[970](#970)        res.ok_or_else(|| Error::UnsupportedCfg(cfg.original().to_string()))
[971](#971)    }

[1101](#1101)    pub fn from_internal_pkg_config<P>(
[1124](#1124)        pkg_config_dir: P,
[1125](#1125)        lib: &str,
[1126](#1126)        version: &str,
[1127](#1127)    ) -> Result<Self, BuildInternalClosureError>

[1129](#1129)        P: AsRef<Path>,
[1130](#1130)    {
[1131](#1131)        let old = env::var("PKG_CONFIG_PATH");
[1133](#1133)
[1134](#1134)        match old {

[1145](#1145)            .atleast_version(version)
[1146](#1146)            .print_system_libs(false)
[1147](#1147)            .cargo_metadata(false)
[1148](#1148)            .statik(true)
[1149](#1149)            .probe(lib);
[1150](#1150)
[1151](#1151)        env::set_var("PKG_CONFIG_PATH", old.unwrap_or_else(|_| "".into()));
[1152](#1152)

[1154](#1154)            Ok(pkg_lib) => {
[1155](#1155)                let mut lib = Self::from_pkg_config(lib, pkg_lib);
[1156](#1156)                lib.statik = true;

# Config in system_deps - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/system-deps/7.0.8/system_deps/struct.Config.html

`pub struct Config { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Structure used to configure `metadata` before starting to probe for dependencies

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/system_deps/lib.rs.html#681-693)#### pub fn [probe](https://docs.rs#method.probe)(self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[Dependencies](https://docs.rs/struct.Dependencies.html), [Error](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/system_deps/lib.rs.html#681-693)

#### pub fn [probe](https://docs.rs#method.probe)(self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[Dependencies](https://docs.rs/struct.Dependencies.html), [Error](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html)>

Probe all libraries configured in the Cargo.toml
`[package.metadata.system-deps]` section.

The returned hash is using the `toml` key defining the dependency as key.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/system_deps/lib.rs.html#707-718)#### pub fn [add_build_internal](https://docs.rs#method.add_build_internal)<F>(self, name: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html), func: F) -> Self

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/system_deps/lib.rs.html#707-718)

#### pub fn [add_build_internal](https://docs.rs#method.add_build_internal)<F>(self, name: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html), func: F) -> Self

Add hook so system-deps can internally build library `name` if requested by user.

It will only be triggered if the environment variable
`SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_BUILD_INTERNAL` is defined with either `always` or
`auto` as value. In the latter case, `func` is called only if the requested
version of the library was not found on the system.

[§](https://docs.rs#arguments)Arguments

- `name`: the name of the library, as defined in- `Cargo.toml`
- `func`: closure called when internally building the library.

It receives as argument the library name, and the minimum version required.

## Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#trait-implementations)

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/system_deps/lib.rs.html#1123-1161)#### pub fn [from_internal_pkg_config](https://docs.rs#method.from_internal_pkg_config)<P>(
    pkg_config_dir: P,
    lib: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
    version: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<Self, [BuildInternalClosureError](https://docs.rs/enum.BuildInternalClosureError.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/system_deps/lib.rs.html#1123-1161)

#### pub fn [from_internal_pkg_config](https://docs.rs#method.from_internal_pkg_config)<P>(
    pkg_config_dir: P,
    lib: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
    version: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<Self, [BuildInternalClosureError](https://docs.rs/enum.BuildInternalClosureError.html)>

Create a `Library` by probing `pkg-config` on an internal directory.
This helper is meant to be used by `Config::add_build_internal` closures
after having built the lib to return the library information to system-deps.

This library will be statically linked.

[§](https://docs.rs#arguments)Arguments

- `pkg_config_dir`: the directory where the library- `.pc`file is located
- `lib`: the name of the library to look for
- `version`: the minimum version of- `lib`required

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
let mut config = system_deps::Config::new();
config.add_build_internal("mylib", |lib, version| {
  // Actually build the library here that fulfills the passed in version requirements
  system_deps::Library::from_internal_pkg_config("build-dir",
      lib, "1.2.4")
});
```

contained an invalid value (allowed: `auto`, `always`, `never`)

`SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_BUILD_INTERNAL=always' or `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_BUILD_INTERNAL=auto’,
but not closure has been defined using `Config::add_build_internal` to build
this lib

The library which has been build internally does not match the
required version defined in `Cargo.toml`

The `cfg()` expression used in `Cargo.toml` is currently not supported

# system_deps - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/system-deps/latest/aarch64-apple-darwin/system_deps/

## Expand description

`system-deps` lets you write system dependencies in `Cargo.toml` metadata,
rather than programmatically in `build.rs`. This makes those dependencies
declarative, so other tools can read them as well.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

In your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[build-dependencies]
system-deps = "2.0"
```
Then, to declare a dependency on `testlib >= 1.2`
add the following section:

```
[package.metadata.system-deps]
testlib = "1.2"
```
Finally, in your `build.rs`, add:

[§](https://docs.rs#version-format)Version format

Versions can be expressed in the following formats

- “1.2” or “>= 1.2”: At least version 1.2
- “>= 1.2, < 2.0”: At least version 1.2 but less than version 2.0

In the future more complicated version expressions might be supported.

Note that these versions are not interpreted according to the semver rules, but based on the rules defined by pkg-config.

[§](https://docs.rs#feature-specific-dependency)Feature-specific dependency

You can easily declare an optional system dependency by associating it with a feature:

```
[package.metadata.system-deps]
testdata = { version = "4.5", feature = "use-testdata" }
```
`system-deps` will check for `testdata` only if the `use-testdata` feature has been enabled.

[§](https://docs.rs#optional-dependency)Optional dependency

Another option is to use the `optional` setting, which can also be used using [features versions](https://docs.rs#feature-versions):

```
[package.metadata.system-deps]
test-data = { version = "4.5", optional = true }
testmore = { version = "2", v3 = { version = "3.0", optional = true }}
```
`system-deps` will automatically export for each dependency a feature `system_deps_have_$DEP` where `$DEP`
is the `toml` key defining the dependency in [snake_case](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snake_case).
This can be used to check if an optional dependency has been found or not:

```
#[cfg(system_deps_have_testdata)]
println!("found test-data");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#overriding-library-name)Overriding library name

`toml` keys cannot contain dot characters so if your library name does, you can define it using the `name` field:

```
[package.metadata.system-deps]
glib = { name = "glib-2.0", version = "2.64" }
```
[§](https://docs.rs#fallback-library-names)Fallback library names

Some libraries may be available under different names on different platforms or distributions. To allow for this, you can define fallback names to search for if the main library name does not work.

```
[package.metadata.system-deps]
aravis = { fallback-names = ["aravis-0.8"] }
```
You may also specify different fallback names for different versions:

```
[package.metadata.system-deps.libfoo]
version = "0.1"
fallback-names = ["libfoo-0.1"]
v1 = { version = "1.0", fallback-names = ["libfoo1"] }
v2 = { version = "2.0", fallback-names = ["libfoo2"] }
```
[§](https://docs.rs#feature-versions)Feature versions

`-sys` crates willing to support various versions of their underlying system libraries
can use features to control the version of the dependency required.
`system-deps` will pick the highest version among enabled features.
Such version features must use the pattern `v1_0`, `v1_2`, etc.

```
[features]
v1_2 = []
v1_4 = ["v1_2"]
v1_6 = ["v1_4"]
[package.metadata.system-deps.gstreamer_1_0]
name = "gstreamer-1.0"
version = "1.0"
v1_2 = { version = "1.2" }
v1_4 = { version = "1.4" }
v1_6 = { version = "1.6" }
```
The same mechanism can be used to require a different library name depending on the version:

```
[package.metadata.system-deps.gst_gl]
name = "gstreamer-gl-1.0"
version = "1.14"
v1_18 = { version = "1.18", name = "gstreamer-gl-egl-1.0" }
```
[§](https://docs.rs#target-specific-dependencies)Target specific dependencies

You can define target specific dependencies:

```
[package.metadata.system-deps.'cfg(target_os = "linux")']
testdata = "1"
[package.metadata.system-deps.'cfg(not(target_os = "macos"))']
testlib = "1"
[package.metadata.system-deps.'cfg(unix)']
testanotherlib = { version = "1", optional = true }
```
See [the Rust documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/conditional-compilation.html)
for the exact syntax.
Currently, those keys are supported:

- `target_arch`
- `target_endian`
- `target_env`
- `target_family`
- `target_os`
- `target_pointer_width`
- `target_vendor`
- `unix`and- `windows`

[§](https://docs.rs#overriding-build-flags)Overriding build flags

By default `system-deps` automatically defines the required build flags for each dependency using the information fetched from `pkg-config`.
These flags can be overridden using environment variables if needed:

- `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_SEARCH_NATIVE`to override the- `cargo:rustc-link-search=native`
- `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_SEARCH_FRAMEWORK`to override the- `cargo:rustc-link-search=framework`
- `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_LIB`to override the- `cargo:rustc-link-lib`
- `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_LIB_FRAMEWORK`to override the- `cargo:rustc-link-lib=framework`
- `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_INCLUDE`to override the- `cargo:include`

With `$NAME` being the upper case name of the key defining the dependency in `Cargo.toml`.
For example `SYSTEM_DEPS_TESTLIB_SEARCH_NATIVE=/opt/lib` could be used to override a dependency named `testlib`.

One can also define the environment variable `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_NO_PKG_CONFIG` to fully disable `pkg-config` lookup
for the given dependency. In this case at least SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_LIB or SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_LIB_FRAMEWORK should be defined as well.

[§](https://docs.rs#internally-build-system-libraries)Internally build system libraries

`-sys` crates can provide support for building and statically link their underlying system library as part of their build process.
Here is how to do this in your `build.rs`:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
fn main() {
    system_deps::Config::new()
        .add_build_internal("testlib", |lib, version| {
            // Actually build the library here that fulfills the passed in version requirements
            system_deps::Library::from_internal_pkg_config("build/path-to-pc-file", lib, "1.2.4")
         })
        .probe()
        .unwrap();
}
```
This feature can be controlled using the `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_BUILD_INTERNAL` environment variable
which can have the following values:

- `auto`: build the dependency only if the required version has not been found by- `pkg-config`;
- `always`: always build the dependency, ignoring any version which may be installed on the system;
- `never`: (default) never build the dependency,- `system-deps`will fail if the required version is not found on the system.

You can also use the `SYSTEM_DEPS_BUILD_INTERNAL` environment variable with the same values
defining the behavior for all the dependencies which don’t have `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_BUILD_INTERNAL` defined.

[§](https://docs.rs#static-linking)Static linking

By default all libraries are dynamically linked, except when build internally as [described above](https://docs.rs#internally-build-system-libraries).
Libraries can be statically linked by defining the environment variable `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_LINK=static`.
You can also use `SYSTEM_DEPS_LINK=static` to statically link all the libraries.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Config](https://docs.rs/struct.Config.html)
- Structure used to configure `metadata`before starting to probe for dependencies
- [Dependencies](https://docs.rs/struct.Dependencies.html)
- All the system dependencies retrieved by `Config::probe`
- [Internal](https://docs.rs/struct.InternalLib.html)- Lib
- Internal library name and if a static library is available on the system
- [Library](https://docs.rs/struct.Library.html)
- A system dependency

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Build](https://docs.rs/enum.BuildInternalClosureError.html)- Internal - Closure - Error
- Error used in return value of `Config::add_build_internal`closures
- [Error](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html)
- system-deps errors
- [Source](https://docs.rs/enum.Source.html)
- From where the library settings have been retrieved

---

# system_deps - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/system-deps/latest/aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu/system_deps/

## Expand description

`system-deps` lets you write system dependencies in `Cargo.toml` metadata,
rather than programmatically in `build.rs`. This makes those dependencies
declarative, so other tools can read them as well.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

In your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[build-dependencies]
system-deps = "2.0"
```
Then, to declare a dependency on `testlib >= 1.2`
add the following section:

```
[package.metadata.system-deps]
testlib = "1.2"
```
Finally, in your `build.rs`, add:

[§](https://docs.rs#version-format)Version format

Versions can be expressed in the following formats

- “1.2” or “>= 1.2”: At least version 1.2
- “>= 1.2, < 2.0”: At least version 1.2 but less than version 2.0

In the future more complicated version expressions might be supported.

Note that these versions are not interpreted according to the semver rules, but based on the rules defined by pkg-config.

[§](https://docs.rs#feature-specific-dependency)Feature-specific dependency

You can easily declare an optional system dependency by associating it with a feature:

```
[package.metadata.system-deps]
testdata = { version = "4.5", feature = "use-testdata" }
```
`system-deps` will check for `testdata` only if the `use-testdata` feature has been enabled.

[§](https://docs.rs#optional-dependency)Optional dependency

Another option is to use the `optional` setting, which can also be used using [features versions](https://docs.rs#feature-versions):

```
[package.metadata.system-deps]
test-data = { version = "4.5", optional = true }
testmore = { version = "2", v3 = { version = "3.0", optional = true }}
```
`system-deps` will automatically export for each dependency a feature `system_deps_have_$DEP` where `$DEP`
is the `toml` key defining the dependency in [snake_case](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snake_case).
This can be used to check if an optional dependency has been found or not:

```
#[cfg(system_deps_have_testdata)]
println!("found test-data");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#overriding-library-name)Overriding library name

`toml` keys cannot contain dot characters so if your library name does, you can define it using the `name` field:

```
[package.metadata.system-deps]
glib = { name = "glib-2.0", version = "2.64" }
```
[§](https://docs.rs#fallback-library-names)Fallback library names

Some libraries may be available under different names on different platforms or distributions. To allow for this, you can define fallback names to search for if the main library name does not work.

```
[package.metadata.system-deps]
aravis = { fallback-names = ["aravis-0.8"] }
```
You may also specify different fallback names for different versions:

```
[package.metadata.system-deps.libfoo]
version = "0.1"
fallback-names = ["libfoo-0.1"]
v1 = { version = "1.0", fallback-names = ["libfoo1"] }
v2 = { version = "2.0", fallback-names = ["libfoo2"] }
```
[§](https://docs.rs#feature-versions)Feature versions

`-sys` crates willing to support various versions of their underlying system libraries
can use features to control the version of the dependency required.
`system-deps` will pick the highest version among enabled features.
Such version features must use the pattern `v1_0`, `v1_2`, etc.

```
[features]
v1_2 = []
v1_4 = ["v1_2"]
v1_6 = ["v1_4"]
[package.metadata.system-deps.gstreamer_1_0]
name = "gstreamer-1.0"
version = "1.0"
v1_2 = { version = "1.2" }
v1_4 = { version = "1.4" }
v1_6 = { version = "1.6" }
```
The same mechanism can be used to require a different library name depending on the version:

```
[package.metadata.system-deps.gst_gl]
name = "gstreamer-gl-1.0"
version = "1.14"
v1_18 = { version = "1.18", name = "gstreamer-gl-egl-1.0" }
```
[§](https://docs.rs#target-specific-dependencies)Target specific dependencies

You can define target specific dependencies:

```
[package.metadata.system-deps.'cfg(target_os = "linux")']
testdata = "1"
[package.metadata.system-deps.'cfg(not(target_os = "macos"))']
testlib = "1"
[package.metadata.system-deps.'cfg(unix)']
testanotherlib = { version = "1", optional = true }
```
See [the Rust documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/conditional-compilation.html)
for the exact syntax.
Currently, those keys are supported:

- `target_arch`
- `target_endian`
- `target_env`
- `target_family`
- `target_os`
- `target_pointer_width`
- `target_vendor`
- `unix`and- `windows`

[§](https://docs.rs#overriding-build-flags)Overriding build flags

By default `system-deps` automatically defines the required build flags for each dependency using the information fetched from `pkg-config`.
These flags can be overridden using environment variables if needed:

- `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_SEARCH_NATIVE`to override the- `cargo:rustc-link-search=native`
- `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_SEARCH_FRAMEWORK`to override the- `cargo:rustc-link-search=framework`
- `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_LIB`to override the- `cargo:rustc-link-lib`
- `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_LIB_FRAMEWORK`to override the- `cargo:rustc-link-lib=framework`
- `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_INCLUDE`to override the- `cargo:include`

With `$NAME` being the upper case name of the key defining the dependency in `Cargo.toml`.
For example `SYSTEM_DEPS_TESTLIB_SEARCH_NATIVE=/opt/lib` could be used to override a dependency named `testlib`.

One can also define the environment variable `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_NO_PKG_CONFIG` to fully disable `pkg-config` lookup
for the given dependency. In this case at least SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_LIB or SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_LIB_FRAMEWORK should be defined as well.

[§](https://docs.rs#internally-build-system-libraries)Internally build system libraries

`-sys` crates can provide support for building and statically link their underlying system library as part of their build process.
Here is how to do this in your `build.rs`:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
fn main() {
    system_deps::Config::new()
        .add_build_internal("testlib", |lib, version| {
            // Actually build the library here that fulfills the passed in version requirements
            system_deps::Library::from_internal_pkg_config("build/path-to-pc-file", lib, "1.2.4")
         })
        .probe()
        .unwrap();
}
```
This feature can be controlled using the `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_BUILD_INTERNAL` environment variable
which can have the following values:

- `auto`: build the dependency only if the required version has not been found by- `pkg-config`;
- `always`: always build the dependency, ignoring any version which may be installed on the system;
- `never`: (default) never build the dependency,- `system-deps`will fail if the required version is not found on the system.

You can also use the `SYSTEM_DEPS_BUILD_INTERNAL` environment variable with the same values
defining the behavior for all the dependencies which don’t have `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_BUILD_INTERNAL` defined.

[§](https://docs.rs#static-linking)Static linking

By default all libraries are dynamically linked, except when build internally as [described above](https://docs.rs#internally-build-system-libraries).
Libraries can be statically linked by defining the environment variable `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_LINK=static`.
You can also use `SYSTEM_DEPS_LINK=static` to statically link all the libraries.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Config](https://docs.rs/struct.Config.html)
- Structure used to configure `metadata`before starting to probe for dependencies
- [Dependencies](https://docs.rs/struct.Dependencies.html)
- All the system dependencies retrieved by `Config::probe`
- [Internal](https://docs.rs/struct.InternalLib.html)- Lib
- Internal library name and if a static library is available on the system
- [Library](https://docs.rs/struct.Library.html)
- A system dependency

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Build](https://docs.rs/enum.BuildInternalClosureError.html)- Internal - Closure - Error
- Error used in return value of `Config::add_build_internal`closures
- [Error](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html)
- system-deps errors
- [Source](https://docs.rs/enum.Source.html)
- From where the library settings have been retrieved

You can define target specific dependencies:

```
[package.metadata.system-deps.'cfg(target_os = "linux")']
testdata = "1"
[package.metadata.system-deps.'cfg(not(target_os = "macos"))']
testlib = "1"
[package.metadata.system-deps.'cfg(unix)']
testanotherlib = { version = "1", optional = true }
```
See [the Rust documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/conditional-compilation.html)
for the exact syntax.
Currently, those keys are supported:

- `target_arch`
- `target_endian`
- `target_env`
- `target_family`
- `target_os`
- `target_pointer_width`
- `target_vendor`
- `unix`and- `windows`

[§](https://docs.rs#overriding-build-flags)Overriding build flags

By default `system-deps` automatically defines the required build flags for each dependency using the information fetched from `pkg-config`.
These flags can be overridden using environment variables if needed:

- `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_SEARCH_NATIVE`to override the- `cargo:rustc-link-search=native`
- `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_SEARCH_FRAMEWORK`to override the- `cargo:rustc-link-search=framework`
- `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_LIB`to override the- `cargo:rustc-link-lib`
- `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_LIB_FRAMEWORK`to override the- `cargo:rustc-link-lib=framework`
- `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_INCLUDE`to override the- `cargo:include`

With `$NAME` being the upper case name of the key defining the dependency in `Cargo.toml`.
For example `SYSTEM_DEPS_TESTLIB_SEARCH_NATIVE=/opt/lib` could be used to override a dependency named `testlib`.

One can also define the environment variable `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_NO_PKG_CONFIG` to fully disable `pkg-config` lookup
for the given dependency. In this case at least SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_LIB or SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_LIB_FRAMEWORK should be defined as well.

[§](https://docs.rs#internally-build-system-libraries)Internally build system libraries

`-sys` crates can provide support for building and statically link their underlying system library as part of their build process.
Here is how to do this in your `build.rs`:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
fn main() {
    system_deps::Config::new()
        .add_build_internal("testlib", |lib, version| {
            // Actually build the library here that fulfills the passed in version requirements
            system_deps::Library::from_internal_pkg_config("build/path-to-pc-file", lib, "1.2.4")
         })
        .probe()
        .unwrap();
}
```
This feature can be controlled using the `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_BUILD_INTERNAL` environment variable
which can have the following values:

- `auto`: build the dependency only if the required version has not been found by- `pkg-config`;
- `always`: always build the dependency, ignoring any version which may be installed on the system;
- `never`: (default) never build the dependency,- `system-deps`will fail if the required version is not found on the system.

You can also use the `SYSTEM_DEPS_BUILD_INTERNAL` environment variable with the same values
defining the behavior for all the dependencies which don’t have `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_BUILD_INTERNAL` defined.

[§](https://docs.rs#static-linking)Static linking

By default all libraries are dynamically linked, except when build internally as [described above](https://docs.rs#internally-build-system-libraries).
Libraries can be statically linked by defining the environment variable `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_LINK=static`.
You can also use `SYSTEM_DEPS_LINK=static` to statically link all the libraries.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Config](https://docs.rs/struct.Config.html)
- Structure used to configure `metadata`before starting to probe for dependencies
- [Dependencies](https://docs.rs/struct.Dependencies.html)
- All the system dependencies retrieved by `Config::probe`
- [Internal](https://docs.rs/struct.InternalLib.html)- Lib
- Internal library name and if a static library is available on the system
- [Library](https://docs.rs/struct.Library.html)
- A system dependency

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Build](https://docs.rs/enum.BuildInternalClosureError.html)- Internal - Closure - Error
- Error used in return value of `Config::add_build_internal`closures
- [Error](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html)
- system-deps errors
- [Source](https://docs.rs/enum.Source.html)
- From where the library settings have been retrieved

# system_deps - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/system-deps/latest/system_deps/

## Expand description

`system-deps` lets you write system dependencies in `Cargo.toml` metadata,
rather than programmatically in `build.rs`. This makes those dependencies
declarative, so other tools can read them as well.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

In your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[build-dependencies]
system-deps = "2.0"
```
Then, to declare a dependency on `testlib >= 1.2`
add the following section:

```
[package.metadata.system-deps]
testlib = "1.2"
```
Finally, in your `build.rs`, add:

[§](https://docs.rs#version-format)Version format

Versions can be expressed in the following formats

- “1.2” or “>= 1.2”: At least version 1.2
- “>= 1.2, < 2.0”: At least version 1.2 but less than version 2.0

In the future more complicated version expressions might be supported.

Note that these versions are not interpreted according to the semver rules, but based on the rules defined by pkg-config.

[§](https://docs.rs#feature-specific-dependency)Feature-specific dependency

You can easily declare an optional system dependency by associating it with a feature:

```
[package.metadata.system-deps]
testdata = { version = "4.5", feature = "use-testdata" }
```
`system-deps` will check for `testdata` only if the `use-testdata` feature has been enabled.

[§](https://docs.rs#optional-dependency)Optional dependency

Another option is to use the `optional` setting, which can also be used using [features versions](https://docs.rs#feature-versions):

```
[package.metadata.system-deps]
test-data = { version = "4.5", optional = true }
testmore = { version = "2", v3 = { version = "3.0", optional = true }}
```
`system-deps` will automatically export for each dependency a feature `system_deps_have_$DEP` where `$DEP`
is the `toml` key defining the dependency in [snake_case](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snake_case).
This can be used to check if an optional dependency has been found or not:

```
#[cfg(system_deps_have_testdata)]
println!("found test-data");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#overriding-library-name)Overriding library name

`toml` keys cannot contain dot characters so if your library name does, you can define it using the `name` field:

```
[package.metadata.system-deps]
glib = { name = "glib-2.0", version = "2.64" }
```
[§](https://docs.rs#fallback-library-names)Fallback library names

Some libraries may be available under different names on different platforms or distributions. To allow for this, you can define fallback names to search for if the main library name does not work.

```
[package.metadata.system-deps]
aravis = { fallback-names = ["aravis-0.8"] }
```
You may also specify different fallback names for different versions:

```
[package.metadata.system-deps.libfoo]
version = "0.1"
fallback-names = ["libfoo-0.1"]
v1 = { version = "1.0", fallback-names = ["libfoo1"] }
v2 = { version = "2.0", fallback-names = ["libfoo2"] }
```
[§](https://docs.rs#feature-versions)Feature versions

`-sys` crates willing to support various versions of their underlying system libraries
can use features to control the version of the dependency required.
`system-deps` will pick the highest version among enabled features.
Such version features must use the pattern `v1_0`, `v1_2`, etc.

```
[features]
v1_2 = []
v1_4 = ["v1_2"]
v1_6 = ["v1_4"]
[package.metadata.system-deps.gstreamer_1_0]
name = "gstreamer-1.0"
version = "1.0"
v1_2 = { version = "1.2" }
v1_4 = { version = "1.4" }
v1_6 = { version = "1.6" }
```
The same mechanism can be used to require a different library name depending on the version:

```
[package.metadata.system-deps.gst_gl]
name = "gstreamer-gl-1.0"
version = "1.14"
v1_18 = { version = "1.18", name = "gstreamer-gl-egl-1.0" }
```
[§](https://docs.rs#target-specific-dependencies)Target specific dependencies

You can define target specific dependencies:

```
[package.metadata.system-deps.'cfg(target_os = "linux")']
testdata = "1"
[package.metadata.system-deps.'cfg(not(target_os = "macos"))']
testlib = "1"
[package.metadata.system-deps.'cfg(unix)']
testanotherlib = { version = "1", optional = true }
```
See [the Rust documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/conditional-compilation.html)
for the exact syntax.
Currently, those keys are supported:

- `target_arch`
- `target_endian`
- `target_env`
- `target_family`
- `target_os`
- `target_pointer_width`
- `target_vendor`
- `unix`and- `windows`

[§](https://docs.rs#overriding-build-flags)Overriding build flags

By default `system-deps` automatically defines the required build flags for each dependency using the information fetched from `pkg-config`.
These flags can be overridden using environment variables if needed:

- `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_SEARCH_NATIVE`to override the- `cargo:rustc-link-search=native`
- `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_SEARCH_FRAMEWORK`to override the- `cargo:rustc-link-search=framework`
- `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_LIB`to override the- `cargo:rustc-link-lib`
- `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_LIB_FRAMEWORK`to override the- `cargo:rustc-link-lib=framework`
- `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_INCLUDE`to override the- `cargo:include`

With `$NAME` being the upper case name of the key defining the dependency in `Cargo.toml`.
For example `SYSTEM_DEPS_TESTLIB_SEARCH_NATIVE=/opt/lib` could be used to override a dependency named `testlib`.

One can also define the environment variable `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_NO_PKG_CONFIG` to fully disable `pkg-config` lookup
for the given dependency. In this case at least SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_LIB or SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_LIB_FRAMEWORK should be defined as well.

[§](https://docs.rs#internally-build-system-libraries)Internally build system libraries

`-sys` crates can provide support for building and statically link their underlying system library as part of their build process.
Here is how to do this in your `build.rs`:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
fn main() {
    system_deps::Config::new()
        .add_build_internal("testlib", |lib, version| {
            // Actually build the library here that fulfills the passed in version requirements
            system_deps::Library::from_internal_pkg_config("build/path-to-pc-file", lib, "1.2.4")
         })
        .probe()
        .unwrap();
}
```
This feature can be controlled using the `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_BUILD_INTERNAL` environment variable
which can have the following values:

- `auto`: build the dependency only if the required version has not been found by- `pkg-config`;
- `always`: always build the dependency, ignoring any version which may be installed on the system;
- `never`: (default) never build the dependency,- `system-deps`will fail if the required version is not found on the system.

You can also use the `SYSTEM_DEPS_BUILD_INTERNAL` environment variable with the same values
defining the behavior for all the dependencies which don’t have `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_BUILD_INTERNAL` defined.

[§](https://docs.rs#static-linking)Static linking

By default all libraries are dynamically linked, except when build internally as [described above](https://docs.rs#internally-build-system-libraries).
Libraries can be statically linked by defining the environment variable `SYSTEM_DEPS_$NAME_LINK=static`.
You can also use `SYSTEM_DEPS_LINK=static` to statically link all the libraries.

# heck 0.5.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/heck/^0.5

**heck** is a case conversion library

This library exists to provide case conversion between common cases like CamelCase and snake_case. It is intended to be unicode aware, internally consistent, and reasonably well performing.

## Definition of a word boundary

Word boundaries are defined by non-alphanumeric characters, as well as within those words in this manner:

- If an uppercase character is followed by lowercase letters, a word boundary is considered to be just prior to that uppercase character.
- If multiple uppercase characters are consecutive, they are considered to be within a single word, except that the last will be part of the next word if it is followed by lowercase characters (see rule 1).

That is, "HelloWorld" is segmented `Hello|World` whereas "XMLHttpRequest" is
segmented `XML|Http|Request`.

Characters not within words (such as spaces, punctuations, and underscores) are not included in the output string except as they are a part of the case being converted to. Multiple adjacent word boundaries (such as a series of underscores) are folded into one. ("hello__world" in snake case is therefore "hello_world", not the exact same string). Leading or trailing word boundary indicators are dropped, except insofar as CamelCase capitalizes the first word.

## Cases contained in this library:

- UpperCamelCase
- lowerCamelCase
- snake_case
- kebab-case
- SHOUTY_SNAKE_CASE
- Title Case
- SHOUTY-KEBAB-CASE
- Train-Case

## MSRV

The minimum supported Rust version for this crate is 1.56.0. This may change in minor or patch releases, but we probably won't ever require a very recent version. If you would like to have a stronger guarantee than that, please open an issue.

## License

heck is distributed under the terms of both the MIT license and the Apache License (Version 2.0).

See LICENSE-APACHE and LICENSE-MIT for details.

# pkg-config 0.3.33 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/pkg-config/^0.3.25

# pkg-config-rs

A simple library meant to be used as a build dependency with Cargo packages in
order to use the system `pkg-config` tool (if available) to determine where a
library is located.

You can use this crate directly to probe for specific libraries, or use
[system-deps](https://github.com/gdesmott/system-deps) to declare all your
`pkg-config` dependencies in `Cargo.toml`.

This library requires Rust 1.31+.

# Example

Find the system library named `foo`, with minimum version 1.2.3:

```
extern crate pkg_config;
```
Find the system library named `foo`, with no version requirement (not
recommended):

```
extern crate pkg_config;
```
# External configuration via target-scoped environment variables

In cross-compilation context, it is useful to manage separately `PKG_CONFIG_PATH`
and a few other variables for the `host` and the `target` platform.

The supported variables are: `PKG_CONFIG_PATH`, `PKG_CONFIG_LIBDIR`, and
`PKG_CONFIG_SYSROOT_DIR`.

Each of these variables can also be supplied with certain prefixes and suffixes, in the following prioritized order:

- `<var>_<target>`- for example,- `PKG_CONFIG_PATH_x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`
- `<var>_<target_with_underscores>`- for example,- `PKG_CONFIG_PATH_x86_64_unknown_linux_gnu`
- `<build-kind>_<var>`- for example,- `HOST_PKG_CONFIG_PATH`or- `TARGET_PKG_CONFIG_PATH`
- `<var>`- a plain- `PKG_CONFIG_PATH`

This crate will allow `pkg-config` to be used in cross-compilation
if `PKG_CONFIG_SYSROOT_DIR` or `PKG_CONFIG` is set. You can set `PKG_CONFIG_ALLOW_CROSS=1`
to bypass the compatibility check, but please note that enabling use of `pkg-config` in
cross-compilation without appropriate sysroot and search paths set is likely to break builds.

Some Rust sys crates support building vendored libraries from source, which may be a work
around for lack of cross-compilation support in `pkg-config`.

# version-compare 0.2.1 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/version-compare/^0.2

# Rust library: version-compare

Rust library to easily compare version numbers with no specific format, and test against various comparison operators.

Comparing version numbers is hard, especially with weird version number formats.

This library helps you to easily compare any kind of version number with no
specific format using a best-effort approach.
Two version numbers can be compared to each other to get a comparison operator
(`<`, `==`, `>`), or test them against a comparison operator.

Along with version comparison, the library provides various other tools for working with version numbers.

Inspired by PHPs [version_compare()](http://php.net/manual/en/function.version-compare.php).

*Note: Still a work in progress. Configurability is currently very limited. Things will change.*

### Formats

Version numbers that would parse successfully include:

`1`, `3.10.4.1`, `1.2.alpha`, `1.2.dev.4`, ` `, ` .   -32 . 1`, `MyApp 3.2.0 / build 0932` ...

See a list of how version numbers compare [here](https://github.com/timvisee/version-compare/blob/411ed7135741ed7cf2fcf4919012fb5412dc122b/src/test.rs#L50-L103).

## Example

This library is very easy to use. Here's a basic usage example:

`Cargo.toml`:

```
[]
 = "0.2"
```
```
use ;
```
See the [ examples](https://docs.rs/examples) directory for more.

## Features

- Compare version numbers, get: `<`,`==`,`>`
- Compare against a comparison operator
(`<`,`<=`,`==`,`!=`,`>=`,`>`)
- Parse complex and unspecified formats
- Static, standalone methods to easily compare version strings in a single line of code

#### Future ideas

- Version ranges
- Support for [npm-style](https://semver.npmjs.com/)operators (e.g.`^1.0`or`~1.0`)
- Manifest: extend `Manifest`for to support a wide set of constraints
- Building blocks for building your own specific version number parser
- Batch comparisons

#### Semver

Version numbers using the [semver](http://semver.org/) format are compared
correctly with no additional configuration.

If your version number strings follow this exact format you may be better off
using the [ semver](https://crates.io/crates/semver) crate for more format
specific features.

If that isn't certain however, `version-compare` makes comparing a breeze.

## Builds

This library is automatically build and tested every day and for each commit using CI services.

See the current status here: [https://gitlab.com/timvisee/version-compare/-/pipelines](https://gitlab.com/timvisee/version-compare/-/pipelines)

## License

This project is released under the MIT license. Check out the [LICENSE](https://docs.rs/LICENSE) file for more information.

# assert_matches 1.5.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/assert_matches/^1.5

# assert_matches

Provides a macro, `assert_matches`, which tests whether a value
matches a given pattern, causing a panic if the match fails.

```
 extern crate assert_matches;
let a = A;
assert_matches!;
assert_matches!;
```
To include in your project, only when tests are compiled, add the following to your Cargo.toml:

```
[]
 = "1.5"
```
And add the following to your crate root:

```

extern crate assert_matches;
```

# lazy_static 1.5.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/lazy_static/^1

# lazy-static.rs

A macro for declaring lazily evaluated statics in Rust.

Using this macro, it is possible to have `static`s that require code to be
executed at runtime in order to be initialized.
This includes anything requiring heap allocations, like vectors or hash maps,
as well as anything that requires non-const function calls to be computed.

## Minimum supported `rustc`

`1.40.0+`

This version is explicitly tested in CI and may only be bumped in new minor versions. Any changes to the supported minimum version will be called out in the release notes.

# Getting Started

[lazy-static.rs is available on crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/lazy_static).
It is recommended to look there for the newest released version, as well as links to the newest builds of the docs.

At the point of the last update of this README, the latest published version could be used like this:

Add the following dependency to your Cargo manifest...

```
[]
 = "1.5.0"
```
...and see the [docs](https://docs.rs/lazy_static) for how to use it.

# Example

```
use lazy_static;
use HashMap;
lazy_static!
```
# Standard library

It is now possible to easily replicate this crate's functionality in Rust's standard library with [ std::sync::OnceLock](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/sync/struct.OnceLock.html). The example above could be also be written as:

```
use HashMap;
use OnceLock;
```

# system-deps 7.0.7 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/system-deps/7.0.7

`system-deps` lets you write system dependencies in `Cargo.toml` metadata,
rather than programmatically in `build.rs`. This makes those dependencies
declarative, so other tools can read them as well.

For now only `pkg-config` dependencies are supported, but we are planning to
[expand it](https://github.com/gdesmott/system-deps/issues/3) at some point.

Users can override dependency flags using environment variables if needed.
`system-deps` also allows `-sys` crates to optionally internally build and
static link the required system library.

`system-deps` has been started as a fork of the
[metadeps](https://github.com/joshtriplett/metadeps) project.

## Documentation

```
[]
 = "2.0"
```
Then, to declare a dependency on `testlib >= 1.2` add the following section:

```
[]
 = "1.2"
```
Finally, in your `build.rs`, add:

```
```
See the [crate documentation](https://docs.rs/system-deps/) for more advanced features.

# system-deps 7.0.6 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/system-deps/7.0.6

`system-deps` lets you write system dependencies in `Cargo.toml` metadata,
rather than programmatically in `build.rs`. This makes those dependencies
declarative, so other tools can read them as well.

For now only `pkg-config` dependencies are supported, but we are planning to
[expand it](https://github.com/gdesmott/system-deps/issues/3) at some point.

Users can override dependency flags using environment variables if needed.
`system-deps` also allows `-sys` crates to optionally internally build and
static link the required system library.

`system-deps` has been started as a fork of the
[metadeps](https://github.com/joshtriplett/metadeps) project.

## Documentation

See the [crate documentation](https://docs.rs/system-deps/).

## Usage

In your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[]
 = "2.0"
```
Then, to declare a dependency on `testlib >= 1.2` add the following section:

```
[]
 = "1.2"
```
Finally, in your `build.rs`, add:

```
```
See the [crate documentation](https://docs.rs/system-deps/) for more advanced features.

---

# system-deps 3.1.2 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/system-deps/3.1.2

`system-deps` lets you write system dependencies in `Cargo.toml` metadata,
rather than programmatically in `build.rs`. This makes those dependencies
declarative, so other tools can read them as well.

For now only `pkg-config` dependencies are supported, but we are planning to
[expand it](https://github.com/gdesmott/system-deps/issues/3) at some point.

Users can override dependency flags using environment variables if needed.
`system-deps` also allows `-sys` crates to optionally internally build and
static link the required system library.

`system-deps` has been started as a fork of the
[metadeps](https://github.com/joshtriplett/metadeps) project.

## Documentation

See the [crate documentation](https://docs.rs/system-deps/).

## Usage

In your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[]
 = "2.0"
```
Then, to declare a dependency on `testlib >= 1.2`
add the following section:

```
[]
 = "1.2"
```
Finally, in your `build.rs`, add:

```
```
See the [crate documentation](https://docs.rs/system-deps/) for more advanced features.

---
